pictures.scene: Jan de Bray, King David Playing the Harp — the king in a white robe with a heavy gold chain and a blue sash, a spiked gold crown set on his yellow turban, his face lifted and his mouth open in song and one hand up among the strings of the harp, a laurel-crowned singer and other musicians pressed in behind him over their books, for the choirmaster according to Gittith, a Psalm of David
pictures.name: pd_de_bray_king_david_playing_the_harp

pictures.scene: Frederic Edwin Church, The Heart of the Andes — the great snow peak standing white over the whole country, the wooded ridges and the wide plain opening away below it, and down in the front a white cross set beside the path where two tiny travellers have stopped and knelt, O LORD our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth
pictures.name: pd_church_the_heart_of_the_andes

pictures.scene: Frederic Edwin Church, Aurora Borealis — the northern lights streaming up the whole dark sky in pale green curtains, a black headland lying under them, and a little ship held fast in the frozen sea below with one lit window and a dog team crossing the ice, You have set Your glory above the heavens
pictures.name: pd_church_aurora

pictures.scene: Jacob Willemsz de Wet, Christ Blessing the Children — Christ seated on the step with the halo faint about His head and His hand laid on His breast, the mothers kneeling in front of Him with babies in their arms and the children crowding up against His knees, one small boy in a red cap sitting on the ground with his back to us, from the mouths of children and infants You have ordained praise
pictures.name: pd_dewet_christus_zegent_kinderen

pictures.scene: Joshua Reynolds, The Infant Samuel — the small child kneeling on the ground in a plain white shift with his hands pressed together and his face turned up into the dark, his lips parted and a faint light breaking in the corner above him, on account of Your adversaries, to silence the enemy and avenger
pictures.name: pd_reynolds_infant_samuel

pictures.scene: Vincent van Gogh, Starry Night over the Rhone — the thick yellow stars burning all over the deep blue sky, the gas lamps along the far bank laying long gold streaks right down the water, and a man and a woman walking arm in arm up the shingle in front, when I behold Your heavens, the work of Your fingers
pictures.name: pd_van_gogh_starry_night_over_the_rhone

pictures.scene: Caspar David Friedrich, Two Men Contemplating the Moon — the two men in long coats standing close together on the bank with their backs to us, one leaning on a staff and the other with a hand on his shoulder, both looking out at the thin crescent moon hanging in the yellow sky, the bare oak branches reaching over their heads, the moon and the stars, which You have set in place
pictures.name: pd_friedrich_two_men_contemplating_the_moon

pictures.scene: Caspar David Friedrich, Wanderer above the Sea of Fog — the man standing alone on the rock with his back to us in a dark green coat, his stick in his hand and his hair blown about, looking out over a whole sea of fog with the ridges and the far peaks standing up out of it, what is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You care for him
pictures.name: pd_friedrich_wanderer_above_the_sea_of_fog

pictures.scene: Matthias Grunewald, The Concert of Angels — the angels kneeling under a great gilded canopy and playing on their viols, the one in front in white with feathered wings drawing his bow and another behind him in flame red, little crowned heads of angels looking out of the dark, and at the side a radiant crowned figure standing in a blaze of gold with her hands lifted, You made him a little lower than the angels, You crowned him with glory and honor
pictures.name: pd_grunewald_the_concert_of_angels

pictures.scene: Rosa Bonheur, Ploughing in the Nivernais — the white oxen leaning into the yoke and coming straight at us through the turned field, the chain drawn tight between them, the ploughman in a blue smock and a broad straw hat walking at their heads with his goad held up, and the broken clods of the new furrow filling the whole front, You made him ruler of the works of Your hands, You have placed everything under his feet
pictures.name: pd_bonheur_ploughing_in_the_nivernais

pictures.scene: Aelbert Cuyp, Cattle near the Maas — the cattle standing and lying together on the river bank under a wide grey sky, the herdsman in a broad straw hat sitting among them with his back to us, two brass milk cans set down on the grass beside him and a sail standing out on the water behind, all sheep and oxen, and even the beasts of the field
pictures.name: pd_cuyp_cattle_near_the_maas

pictures.scene: Bruno Liljefors, Sea Eagles — the two sea eagles out over the open water, one dropping in on them with its wings thrown up and its talons reaching, the other already down on the waves with the fish in its claws, the grey squall standing up behind them, the birds of the air and the fish of the sea, all that swim the paths of the seas
pictures.name: pd_liljefors_sea_eagles

pictures.scene: Thomas Moran, Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone — the great gorge opening away under a clouded sky, the falls coming down white into it at the head and the river winding on below between the pinnacles, the cliffs on either hand burning yellow and rose in the light, O LORD our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth
pictures.name: pd_moran_grand_canyon_of_the_yellowstone

lines.text: For the choirmaster. According to Gittith.
A Psalm of David.
O LORD, our Lord,
how majestic is Your name in all the earth!
You have set Your glory
above the heavens.
From the mouths of children and infants
You have ordained praise
on account of Your adversaries,
to silence the enemy and avenger.
When I behold Your heavens,
the work of Your fingers,
the moon and the stars,
which You have set in place—
what is man that You are mindful of him,
or the son of man that You care for him?
You made him a little lower than the angels;
You crowned him with glory and honor.
You made him ruler of the works of Your hands;
You have placed everything under his feet:
all sheep and oxen,
and even the beasts of the field,
the birds of the air and the fish of the sea,
all that swim the paths of the seas.
O LORD, our Lord,
how majestic is Your name in all the earth!
